name: Stoning To Death
overview: The Scriptures reveal that stoning to death was a divinely mandated form of capital punishment for certain grievous sins and acts of rebellion against God's holy standards. Offenses such as profaning the Sabbath (Exodus 31:15), idolatry involving Molech (Leviticus 20:2), sexual immorality (Leviticus 20:13), occult practices (Leviticus 20:27), and blasphemy against the name of the LORD (Leviticus 24:16) were met with this severe judgment, underscoring the holiness of God and the seriousness of sin. Even familial rebellion, as seen in the case of a stubborn son (Deuteronomy 21:18), was addressed within this framework, reflecting the call to uphold God's order in both community and family life.
